subject: Request: remit override + invoice split for Nebula Health (Order Form redlines)
messages:
From: Claire Holt <claire.holt@nebulahealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nebulahealth.com>, Marco Bianchi <marco@legal-consultants.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Remit override request + invoice split for upcoming order form

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to confirm a couple of operational items for the upcoming order form before we sign:

- We need the invoice to be split across two legal entities: Nebula Health UK Ltd (for EU purchases) and Nebula Health US Inc (for non-EU). PO numbers will arrive from both entities.
- Net terms: finance is asking for Net 60 for UK entity and Net 45 for US entity.
- Tax evidence: legal wants confirmation you can accept VAT reverse-charge where applicable and a path for withheld VAT evidence.

Attached is a draft PO and our preferred invoice remit addresses. Can Redwood accept a remit override so that invoices are routed to the appropriate entity based on SKU or pricing tranche? If not, what alternatives (split order form appendix, separate order forms, or remit override mapping table) are possible?

We’re aiming to execute this week — any quick guidance appreciated.

Best,
Claire
Claire Holt
Head of Procurement
Nebula Health
T: +44 20 5555 0198

Attachments: NEB_PO_4552.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Remit override request + invoice split for upcoming order form

Team — forwarding Nebula’s ask. Key asks: invoice routing to two entities, mixed net terms, VAT / reverse-charge handling. I’ve attached Nebula’s PO and a quick redline to the Order Form that proposes an "Invoice Remit Mapping" appendix (page 3) that would allow us to route invoices by product band/price tranche.

Asks:
- Kimberly: can Finance accept remit override mapping operationally? What will this do to collections and AR?
- Ben: pricing chair — does splitting invoices by tranche cause recognition or billing cadence issues? Does minimum commit segmentation need an amendment?
- Jonas: Legal — see my inline redlines. Is adding an appendix acceptable (simpler than two separate order forms)? Any compliance or MSA concerns re: multi-entity invoicing?

I recommend we keep the MSA as-is and add an Order Form appendix; that preserves signatures and avoids re-executing the MSA. If anyone prefers a separate order form per entity tell me now.

Thanks — I’m in catch-all mode this morning and can hop on a quick call.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Remit override request + invoice split for upcoming order form

Sofia / Kim — quick read from pricing/ops:

- Splitting invoices by pricing tranche is feasible if we can deterministically map SKUs/price bands to remit addresses. The attached pricing_tranche_table.xlsx is my proposed mapping (tranche A = UK entity, tranche B = US entity).
- Minimum commit: if we route revenue across entities we need the order form to state whether the minimum commit is aggregated (company-level) or per-entity. Nebula implied they want the minimum to sit at the group level, but their PO flow treats each entity separately. That mismatch will impact billing triggers and termination rights. Recommend we add language: "Minimum Commit: aggregated across entities unless otherwise specified in a signed appendix."
- Net terms: Finance note — Net 60 for UK + Net 45 for US is OK but requires PO-level tagging. If Nebula can provide entity-specific POs, we can honor mixed terms. However, we cannot accept a single invoice with multiple due dates. Each invoice must carry a single due date; split invoices per remit entity solves that.

Operational asks for Procurement: please get entity-specific PO numbers and VAT IDs. Also ask for the VAT residency certs — we need that to enable reverse-charge treatment and to support bookkeeping.

If Legal is comfortable with an appendix flow, I’ll confirm the billing system changes (small config) and provide an ops runbook.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_tranche_table.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Holt <claire.holt@nebulahealth.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nebulahealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marco Bianchi <marco@legal-consultants.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Remit override request + invoice split for upcoming order form

Claire / Sofia — thanks for the clear summary. From Legal’s side:

- Appendix approach: acceptable and preferred. I attached a short draft appendix clause that we can append to the Order Form titled "Appendix A: Invoice Remit Mapping and Entity Allocation." Key points: it acknowledges multi-entity remit, sets the minimum commit aggregation clause ("Group aggregated unless appendix states otherwise"), and confirms that each invoice will be issued to a single legal entity with the due date tied to that entity’s terms.
- Taxes: we will accept Nebula’s VAT certificates and rely on their evidence to support reverse-charge where applicable. The appendix will require Nebula to supply VAT IDs and residency certificates at execution. Redline language includes a 30-day evidence window; if evidence is not provided within 30 days Redwood may reclassify tax treatment and revert to gross invoicing plus VAT.
- Execution: to keep signatures clean, we propose 1) add Appendix A to the Order Form PDF, 2) upload to DocuSign as an amendment to the existing MSA/order form envelope, and 3) require entity-specific PO numbers in the DocuSign fields where applicable.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- Today EOD: Sofia to send Nebula the redline with Appendix A (I’ll attach the draft below).
- Tomorrow AM: Nebula to confirm PO numbers and upload VAT certs.
- Tomorrow EOD: Send amended Order Form via DocuSign.

Claire — I copied Marco in case Nebula wants legal review. If you’re ok I’ll draft the appendix and Sofia can send the DocuSign link.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: AppendixA_InvoiceRemitMapping_draft.docx (document), NEB_OrderForm_Redline_20260803.pdf (pdf)
